explained.headline: US envoys pledge European presence in upcoming Russia-Ukraine peace talks

happened.text: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to Moscow and Dublin, where they announced that European delegates would be included in the next round of peace talks with Russia.

background.text: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and about one-fifth of Ukraine remains under Russian occupation.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are advisers to US President Donald Trump, operating as special intermediaries in ongoing shuttle diplomacy.
Prior to the Dublin meetings, negotiations were held in Abu Dhabi without direct European participation in talks with the Russian delegation.

matters.text: Kaja Kallas stated that the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin had realised Europe is a major player.
European leaders fear the US might accept Russian demands regarding regional security structures in exchange for a seat at the negotiating table.

uncertain.text: Kaja Kallas expressed doubts as to whether there is genuine Russian momentum toward achieving a peace deal.
European Union institutions have not yet decided on a single central figure to represent them in future talks.
Details regarding the exact timing and total number of prisoners to be included in the announced exchange remain unspecified.

removed.text: During their diplomatic tour, the US negotiators also met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and agreed with Russia and Ukraine on plans for a large prisoner exchange.

explained.headline: Global Microsoft outage disrupts email and workplace software

happened.text: Microsoft stated that its initial repair efforts did not progress as expected because restarted servers became unresponsive again upon receiving traffic.

background.text: Microsoft is a US software giant whose Microsoft 365 cloud-based subscription service is used by more than 430 million people globally.
The disruption also affected third-party integrations relied upon by artificial intelligence firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

matters.text: Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at the trading platform eToro, explained that repeated outages could damage customer trust in Microsoft over the long term.

IT security expert Dennis-Kenji Kipker stated in an interview that companies and public authorities have become highly vulnerable and suffer a loss of control by outsourcing software to cloud services.
Mark Gregory, an associate professor at RMIT University, noted that businesses reliant on cloud services ought to maintain backup options.

uncertain.text: Microsoft has not published a definitive root cause for the server failures, though the company stated there was no indication of a cyberattack.
The exact total number of affected users remains unconfirmed by the tech company.
It remains unclear precisely when all Microsoft 365 services will be fully restored without restriction.

The simulation of human intelligence processes by machines and computer systems.

removed.text: Microsoft experienced a global outage that affected millions of users across 74 countries and disrupted services including Outlook and Teams for more than 12 hours.

The disruption affected diverse international organizations, including pharmacy communications with general practitioner surgeries in the UK, flight support services in India, and government systems in Singapore and Japan.
why: Evidence does not mention UK pharmacy communications or Indian flight support services.

also.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy

explained.headline: US lawmakers summon Nvidia former chief and commerce secretary over scandal

happened.text: Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs.
US Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott requested that Jensen Huang and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appear at a public hearing on December 3.
Three House committees have also summoned Jensen Huang, Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter and Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler for separate hearings.

background.text: Howard Lutnick serves as the United States commerce secretary within Donald Trump's administration.
US authorities suspect a woman named Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang had a relationship, of spying for China, though China denies the allegation.

matters.text: Chinese authorities warned that tightening US regulations on semiconductor exports would threaten the stability of global industry and supply chains.
Republican senator John Cornyn stated that there needed to be a thorough investigation and accountability for the circumvention of national security export controls.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer stated that Jensen Huang and Nvidia must answer whether America's security had been jeopardised.

uncertain.text: White House officials are discussing whether Howard Lutnick should be dismissed from his position.
Democratic lawmakers are questioning what President Donald Trump knew and when he learned about Jensen Huang's relationship.
It remains to be seen whether Jensen Huang will appear voluntarily before congressional committees or face formal subpoenas.
